## C1212b CMV N1c fix (b2384; 2026-11-13T10:11:59Z)
- Small FIX. Returning the stored keep on every later call in the round ignores that call's group and x. If a later publish carries a different group (a re-pick), or the round's FIRST call ran before the stance (publish_task at brain_turn.cc:8 runs at turn start), the stored keep forces an engaged claim on the wrong group or fails to keep the right one. Form: advance the streak once per round (on the round's first stance call), but evaluate keep on EVERY call from that call's x and group: keep = stance(x) && group == cmvc_eng_g && near && streak <= 2. Update cmvc_eng_g only on the round's LAST call, or set it from each call (the last write wins, as it is the published claim).

## C1219 HOX bits 2/4 (b2386 nova_b2386_hoo on v887; 2026-11-13T10:15:22Z)
- FIX (shared-input election, C1076/C980): hox_mate_owns is a team election, deciding who takes a home group, but its inputs are each body's own: mine = travel[gi] (my travel table), while a seen mate's walk = the group field at its position, else cheb x 5/4, and unseen mates are ignored unless they claim gi.
  - (a) Metric mismatch: A rates itself by travel and rates B by the group field; B does the reverse. Both can see the other as nearer and BOTH skip the group.
  - (b) Vision asymmetry: A sees B and skips; B doesn't see A. That part is consistent (B takes it), but if B then re-picks elsewhere, nobody takes it. That is the convergence gap (MGY4: re-picks 70-89%).
  - Fix: use ONE metric for everyone. The group field at each body's position, with my own position used for me, is symmetric when both are seen. Treat 'unseen and not claiming' as not racing, as now. Also add an expiry: if no mate's claim names gi within ~3 rounds of my skip, I stop skipping it. Shared claims are the only common truth.
- FIX: a seen mate posting NO group is counted as a racer, but no group also covers stance/fight codes (claim_x >= 100: fighting or retreating) and bank/tribute walks. Those mates are not going to the home group, so nobody farms it. Count only mates whose published state is idle/choosing (no stance code), or that claim gi.
- Bit 4: CORRECT as a one-sided choice (earliest home respawn with wait < travel to b, not mate-owned, reachable; out_rate unchanged so the retarget switch rule applies). NOTE: respawn_at is own memory, possibly estimated. If the wait at the group ends with the group not alive (wrong estimate), check target_turn_wait_for_respawn's bail.

A MATE that hit the camp on its turn and then walked out of range + 2, or one hitting with a spell whose range exceeds range + 2, reads as an unseen hitter, and the Prism drops a group her own team is clearing. When she is on one and I step off, the region stays held.

## C1273 DBU bit 32 'double from round, team and priority' (Planner rule; b2399; 2026-11-13T12:05:15Z): CORRECT, as a TEAM-level double.
- The model (INT:14-16; GR:126-130; engine-confirmed in replays): each round the teams interleave one body at a time, starting team first, each team sorted by its own priorities (ties by id). When one team runs out, the other's remaining bodies act in order. Dead bodies keep their place (INT:17), so the sizes A (ours) and B (theirs) count the dead too.
- Foe turns between my turn in R and my turn in R+1 depend only on positions, so foe priorities don't matter for 'does ANY foe act in between'. Let k = my rank in our team in R, k' = my rank in R+1.
  - We start R (so they start R+1): foes after me in R = B - min(k, B); foes before me in R+1 = min(k' + 1, B). The total is 0 only if B = 0. So there is NO double on a round we start.
  - They start R (so we start R+1): foes after me in R = B - min(k + 1, B); foes before me in R+1 = min(k', B). The total is 0 iff k >= B - 1 AND k' = 0.
- So a team double exists only on rounds where the ENEMY starts (round parity, enemy_starts(R)), for a body ranked at or past B - 1 in R (after every foe body) and ranked 0 in R+1. Unequal sizes: if A < B, k <= A - 1 < B - 1, so NO double is possible for us. If A = B, it needs k = A - 1 (last) in R, then first in R+1, which is a priority change between the rounds (set_priority applies next round, GR 'set_priority'). If A > B, any of our bodies at rank >= B - 1 qualifies.
- Limits to state:
  - (i) This is the strict, team-level double (no foe at all in between). DBU's original 'double v the foes within 6' can hold more often, and that one does depend on specific foes' ranks (AOT/C1224).
  - (ii) k' needs every mate's NEXT-round priority. Unseen mates read rc 97 (INT:21), so use AOT's last-known cache. A body can only be sure of its own value, so a mate's late priority change can move k'.

## C1273b DBU pairwise double (Planner's owner-asked form; b2399; 2026-11-13T12:08:23Z)
- Slot formula: CORRECT (INT:14-16, GR:126-130), 1-based, m = min(sizes), dead bodies counted. Starting team: r <= m -> 2r - 1, else 2m + (r - m). Second team: r <= m -> 2r, else 2m + (r - m). Only the larger team can have r > m, and its extra bodies follow the 2m interleaved slots in order.
- Pairwise test 's(f,R) < s(b,R) and s(f,R+1) > s(b,R+1)': CORRECT. With equal sizes and UNCHANGED ranks it reduces to rank_b == rank_f with the foe starting R (I checked both parities: when we start R the two conditions contradict).
- set_priority takes effect from the NEXT round (GameRules 'Who goes first'; INT:18-21: prev_priority() is the value in force this round, priority() the next round's for a body that has acted). So use the R ranks from in-force values and the R+1 ranks from next-round values; a rank can differ between R and R+1.
- FIX 1 (foe rank): priority() of one seen foe is its priority VALUE, not its RANK. Its rank needs every foe's priority (unseen foes read rc 97). Use the AOT roster ranking with the last-known cache (C1224b) for rf (R) and rf' (R+1). For R+1, priority() is exact only for a foe that has already acted this round (state & 32, INT:20-21); before its turn it can still change, so the read may break exactly as the Builder asks. Treat a not-yet-acted foe's R+1 rank as unknown (no double claimed), or use the cache.
- FIX 2 (our rank): P.prio[slot] is the BASE order. Live adopts dynamic priorities each turn (turn_order_base - 7 x fq, the finish 35 / lethal 40 overrides, Issac's tie, adopt_prio). Our rank in R must come from in-force values (prev_priority of seen mates, the AOT cache for unseen ones, PRA_DEC-decoded), and in R+1 from my cur_prio plus mates' next values (aot_rank_me's form).

## C1296 PDT pre-build questions (b2402, spec_pdt_1113; 2026-11-13T14:22:10Z)
- (1) k = still_to_act(rb + miss) + first_next_round(rb2) is the right 'foe turns before my next turn' (the foe_turns_within_rounds(e, 2) form, from the turn_order_ranks ranks; alternation by enemy_starts). It can also be wrong when:
  - (a) MY next-round rank moves after k is computed: my own set_dynamic_turn_priority writes later in the turn (35 / 40 overrides, the fq tiers). Compute k after my priority for next round is final, or from the value I will write.
  - (b) An unseen MATE's priority is read as 0 (rc 97, INT:21), which shifts my rank among ours: use the AOT last-known cache (C1224b).
  - (c) Dead bodies keep their place (INT:17): they must be in both rosters.
- (2) Yes to both. At k = 0, a tile within her range 4 but outside his ONE-turn reach makes a wrong k = 1 cost no hit. Use combat::foe_next_turn_reach(e) (kit- and slot-aware: a walking-compatible dash adds 2, GR:159-161; spells at range 4 with radius 1; a ranged basic can't follow a walk, rc 41 / GR:100). Not 'range + 1'. At k = 2, outside his TWO-turn reach is enough: under the interleaving he gets at most 2 turns before my next, since a body can't act twice in a round (GR:124-130). The residual risk is a k computed as 0 that is really 2 (two rank errors at once); state it.
- (3) Bush: basic attacks and ENEMY-TARGETED spells need the target in the attacker's own vision or his own ward's; otherwise the engine refuses (rc 42 attacks, rc 30 casts, INT:199). So a foe outside her bush cluster, with no vision into it (GR:351-355: a bush is opaque from outside) and no ward lighting it, cannot target her. Three exceptions:
  - (i) A GROUND-targeted area spell (Prism / Stellar-type slot 1, 'Target: Ground') aimed at her remembered tile is not a unit target, so it can still land on her.
  - (ii) A foe that steps INTO her cluster sees the whole cluster at once. A melee foe can then walk + hit in the same turn (GR:100-102).
  - (iii) His ward placed in or lighting the cluster gives him vision the same turn (INT:194).
  So 'bush' is safe against ranged basics and targeted spells, but not against a melee walk-in, an area spell or a ward.

## C1301 HMX heal units (VV, spec_hmx_1113; live v897; 2026-11-13T14:36:51Z): CONFIRMED units mismatch, behaviour lane.
- (1) The budget is EFFECTIVE health: x.budget = max(0, hp - CAL_TAB[10]% maxhp) / max(.3, camp_mult) (econ_team_model.cc:165; budget_he rescaled in build_team, :166), so HP divided by the body's camp-damage multiplier (Jungle .70, Durability .90, both .63). tfe_feasible compares RAW camp damage with it (econ_rate.cc:452-535, budget :502-513), so damage and budget are consistent in raw units. But heal and shield are subtracted from the raw damage 1:1 (econ_rate.cc:494). A heal restores HP, and on a body with multiplier m one restored HP absorbs 1/m raw damage, so the heal is under-credited by 1/m (x1.43 Jungle, x1.59 both): the owner's point is right.
- (2) The same in estimate_cx: econ_clear_estimate.cc:143 subtracts (heal8 + shield8) / cooldown x tc raw, against the same per-body budget (:156-172). The siege gates (SG_MARGIN / SG_MARGIN_CALL, econ_team_ops) read estimate_cx's e.dmg v e.budget, so they inherit it.
- (3) heal8 (econ_rate.cc:416-421) sums each crew body's x.heal = heal_mod x CURRENT Focus (econ_team_model.cc:146; Willow 3 x Focus) per slot cooldown, and only once the crew has >= 2 bodies: the first body's heal is held in heal_first and added when a second joins, so a solo Willow's self-heal is never credited. shield8 is the first body's (the tank's) shield only.
- Fix form for HMX: divide the heal credit by the RECEIVING body's multiplier (the tank, cb[0]'s camp_mult). ## C1311 LGP bits 1/2 (b2392 nova_b2392_lgp on v898, spec_lgp_1113, owner replay 01a1d559; 2026-11-13T15:00:06Z): (a) OK, (b) FIX bit 2, (c) FIX.

  - The mate never waits (value 0, so it takes the next target).
- (b) FIX, bit 2 bound (X912 BNX pattern): bit 2 multiplies HER row's value by LGP_K/100 = 3.0 in rate_for (single and pair rows). Neither group_bounds copy (econ_choose_target.cc ~:330 / ~:757) nor group_bounds_finish carries it: there is no LGP site in econ_choose_target.cc. group_value doesn't carry it either (the factor is applied after it), so even the gv_exact path misses it.

  - Fix: in both copies, ub *= LGP_K/100 when self == prism_slot() and the group is a safe cluster by the static test (n_att == 0, n_clu > 0, gems > 0). That's an upper bound: dropping the state conditions only loosens it.

  - her Body from W.ally_by_slot (her position, hp, channelling; if I don't see her, the factor is 1).
  - Two bodies that see differently value a mate's (or her) row differently, so the team model and the claims diverge.
  - Simplest fix for the deadline: apply both bits only on my own row (self == my_slot(); bit 2 then means she is me). One-sided, like TGP/RCR: mates' rows of me ignore it, and claims settle it.
  - Alternative: for mates' rows use only shared inputs (team table, her claim cgroup(ps) and its anchor, shared foe reports).
- Minor: the pair row passes the single row's t as mate_t; t2 is the pair trip's time. Use t2 there.

## C1331 PMM bit 16 DOUBLE-TURN STUN (b2392 nova_b2392_pmm16 on v901; 2026-11-13T16:05:48Z): formulas CORRECT for full visibility; 2 FIXes.
- Parity: interleave positions (INT:14), with ours at 2k when we start and 2k+1 otherwise. Checked:
  - 'foe after me this round': we_start ? rb >= ra : rb > ra.
  - 'foe before her next round' (the other team starts then): we_start ? rb2 <= rh2 : rb2 < rh2.
  - 'she acted': rh < ra.
  - Caveats: unequal team sizes (INT:15: the larger team's extra bodies act after) shift positions past the smaller team's count. Dead bodies keep their place (INT:17).
- Mechanism: right. Stunning a foe that hasn't acted removes this round's turn, and it can then act first next round (INT:40, INT:42). So its two turns before her next become one, which is the owner's intent.
- Two-turn reach max(r1, 2 r1 - range) is a sound upper bound: two moves plus one range (INT:31-32 reaches). It overcounts when the dash is on cooldown for the second turn, which only spends a stun more often. Fine.
- FIX 1 (exactness, rules-gaps M1): ranks from priority reads count only VISIBLE bodies, and priority reads need vision (rc 97, INT:18). Unseen mates or foes, and dead bodies (INT:17), shift ranks, and tied priorities are wrongly broken.
  - Use the exact has-acted bit for the current round (state & 32, exact for mates and seen foes, INT:21): 'she acted' = her state & 32; 'foe not acted' = !(e.state & 32).
  - Keep ranks only for the next-round comparison. For a seen foe that has acted, priority() returns its next-round value exactly (INT:22).
- FIX 2 (rule): skip stun-immune foes. Marcella's passive makes her immune to stuns (GR:656). A cast on her is wasted (combat_cast.cc:617 already treats a stun-immune focus specially). Add the same immune test to the target filter (econ_retarget.cc ~:667).
- Order: turn_tail after the fight stage, with !W.cast, so a kill cast goes first (one cast per turn, GR:118). Fine.

## C1333 DLQ bits 1/2 (b2402 nova_b2402_dlk on v901, owner replay 01a1d594; 2026-11-13T16:08:16Z): bit 1 CORRECT; bit 2 FIX (the kill test is the wrong bar for stunnable channellers).

## C1392 SHV bits 1/2 (b2429 nova_b2429_shv on v907, spawn-heal clears; 2026-11-13T18:56:57Z): basis right; FIX for bit 1.
- Basis: a body on its OWN spawn tile heals to full at its turn end (GR:124/387; INT:7). Camp turns run at round start, before champion turns (GR:124). So a body standing on our spawn within reach of a monolith / golem takes each round's hits, then is healed at its own turn end.
  - Damage accumulates only WITHIN one round: it survives iff the hits landing between two of its turn ends stay under HP + shield. Over a whole clear the net damage is ~0, as long as no single round's incoming kills it.
- FIX (bit 1, the zeroing of e.dmg at econ_clear_estimate.cc:157 and tfe_feasible:505): two gaps.
  - (i) It zeroes the WHOLE crew's damage, though only bodies actually standing on a spawn tile heal. The tank or a melee body off the spawn (attacking from a non-spawn tile) still takes real damage.
  - (ii) It has no per-round lethality test. A monolith hits for 200 (GR:188) per attacker turn, x camp mult, so a light body on spawn can die inside one round.
  - Zero the damage only when (a) every crew body that the attackers reach stands on a spawn tile within its own attack range of the group (the shv_crew_reach class), AND (b) the max per-round incoming on the tank (attackers in reach x str x cm) < its HP + shield.
  - Bit 2 already has (b) ('no bail while incoming < hp'). Copy it into bit 1.
- Bit 2's walk goals and no-bail on the own spawn tile are fine with (b). The 'maxhp > group str_sum' precondition is the right idea. Static class (GR:254 spawn tiles), state-keyed.

## C1397 KID bits 1/2 (b2379 nova_b2379_kid on v908, Shared Mem parity double; 2026-11-13T19:00:19Z): CORRECT as a conservative guard, one precision note.
- (2) Yes. A visible foe's state & 32 is the exact has-completed-turn bit (INT:21, b2263 probe). Unseen foes read rc 97 and are rightly skipped.
- (1) enemy_starts(round + 1) is necessary, but not sufficient, for a double. Teams alternate one body at a time and the starter swaps each round (INT:14, GR:126-130). With ranks within each team:
  - this round we start (so they start next): the foe acts after me now iff rb >= ra, and before me next round iff rb <= ra. So a DOUBLE needs rb == ra (plus the unequal-size and dead-body shifts, INT:15/17);
  - this round they start: after me now needs rb > ra, before me next needs rb < ra. No double.
  - So 'unacted + their team starts next' also flags every unacted foe with rb > ra, which acts after me next round too: over-counting. That's SAFE (extra step-outs, no missed doubles).
  - If the step-out count looks high, tighten with the PMM16 form (C1331): ranks from next-round priorities, and a seen foe that has acted returns its next-round priority exactly (INT:22). Unacted foes' ranks are visibility-limited (rules-gaps M1).
- (3) The departure (only before the farm step) is fine. The step-out tile is priced with danger_veto < eff_hp, the lowest chosen.

## C1398 DNP bits 1/2 (b2418 nova_b2418_dnp on v908, a rich Prism takes no deny walk; 2026-11-13T19:01:10Z): CORRECT, answers.

## C1404 HGL bit 1 (b2420 nova_b2420_hgl on v908, Deep spec_hgl_1113; 2026-11-13T19:10:39Z): 2 FIXes.

Two bodies can hold different gold weights at once, so the team model and the claims diverge.

## C1438 (2026-11-13T19:48:18Z): b2390 HND (capture hand-off) on v909: FIX-FIRST; DUPLICATES b2407 CHX (C1406)
- HND is the same mechanism as CHX: holder leaves / claimant waits, by shy_rank, no foe within CL_FOE. CHX already carries the C1395 timing fix and a wait cap (CHX_WAIT 3). chx1b was skipped at 19:26Z as 'not built on live' after v909 and needs a v909 re-arm. Don't arm both.

The region is then empty at the next round-start capture phase (GR:124) and progress resets (GR:196). Required, as in CHX: when no other mate holds a member tile, the claimant is cheb <= 1 from my tile and hasn't acted this round (state & 32 == 0, exact for visible bodies, INT:21). With another mate on the region, the region stays occupied and 'within 2' is fine.
- Q2: (b) is bounded by the capture resolving (paid by R+6, INT:120) or the holder leaving. A cap like CHX_WAIT is still safer, because ranks are computed from each body's own sight (frac, shards_of), so holder and claimant can disagree on who out-ranks whom. The claimant then waits while the holder never leaves (the holder's view says it out-ranks the claimant).
- Q3: shy_rank on both sides with the slot tie-break is symmetric if both see the same frac and shards. Bodies within 2 normally see each other, so the disagreement is rare.
- Recommendation: re-arm chx1b on v909 and drop HND, or port CHX's C1395 test and wait cap into HND.

## C1538 (2026-11-13T22:09:45Z): b2384 TOW (target-owner stamp; X929 follow-up) DESIGN review, before the build: three changes
- The counts: squad <-> apply is ~1.1 / g, the real cross-setter flip. Route <-> squad is 0 and route <-> apply ~.03 / g. apply -> apply at 4.13 is an upper bound from the stale label.
- 1 (stale label): set tow_who in a scope guard around each setter site (reset to 0 when the site returns), not only at entry. Otherwise a later set_target from an unrelated path inherits 'apply' and is wrongly allowed or blocked. Re-count apply -> apply with the fixed label before deciding anything about it.
- 2 (callers that assume success): don't block owner 0 ('other'). Paths such as siege_try_call, bank / shop errands and the opening keeps call set_target and then assume T.target changed (SGO.gi / T.* bookkeeping). Silently refusing them creates exactly the decider / executor mismatch TOW is meant to remove. Gate only the four named setters against each other, or make set_target return a bool and audit every caller.
- 3 (scope): TOW doesn't touch same-owner flips. If the fixed apply -> apply count is real, it needs hysteresis inside apply_retarget_choice (the switch margin / eval_round), not an owner stamp.
- Otherwise sound: a 1-round span (an emergency switch is at most 1 round late), sets from -1 always pass, and death / capture / flee go through drop_target.

## C1539 (2026-11-13T22:10:04Z): b2384 TOW diff (tow1v) on v911: FIX-FIRST (C1538 items 1 + 2 not applied; the diff crossed my design note)
- tow.diff:27 blocks any who != tow_owner, including who == 0, so siege_try_call, the errands and the opening keeps (unlabeled set_target callers that then assume the change happened) are silently refused within 1 round of a labeled change. That is a decider / executor mismatch (C1538-2). Fix: block only when who != 0 && tow_owner != 0 && who != tow_owner.
- tow.diff:80 sets tow_who = 3 at apply_retarget_choice's ENTRY, and it is cleared only by the next set_target (:23-24). If apply returns without setting, the next unrelated set_target (any caller, possibly turns later) runs as 'apply' (C1538-1). Fix: reset tow_who = 0 on every return path of the labeled sites (a small RAII guard), or set it immediately before apply's own set_target call(s).
- The rest is correct: a blocked set returns before T.rate / crew / eval_round, sets from -1 pass, the span is 1 round, and the flag is read first.
